lessons.title: Personal and Psychological Importance of Religion
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Religion is an organized system of beliefs and worship whose foundation is the divine message. It teaches a person the principles of living, high moral values and the difference between right and wrong, and gives him peace and contentment. Psychology is the science of the human mind and behaviour. This lesson explains what religion and psychology are, how religious upbringing differs from ordinary upbringing, and how religion and psychology both affect a person's thinking and behaviour.

Important Points

  • Religion is an organized system of beliefs and worship, founded on the divine message.
  • Religion teaches the principles of living, high moral values and the difference between right and wrong.
  • Psychology is the science of the human mind and behaviour; it helps us understand thoughts, feelings, emotions and reactions.
  • The blessing of intellect, understanding and perception has been given to man.
  • Religious upbringing is based on principles and teaches a person to understand the beliefs of others correctly; ordinary upbringing lacks this religious guidance.
  • Religious upbringing broadens a person's thinking and makes him a friend to every human being.
  • Religion and psychology basically affect a person's thinking and behaviour.

Religion and Psychology — The Difference

  • Religion helps with moral principles and rules; psychology helps in understanding feelings and emotions.
  • Religion shows a person the purpose of life and teaches gratitude for the blessings of the True Owner; psychology teaches a person to live according to his conscience and society.
  • Religion gives a person spiritual peace; psychology helps in understanding the problems of life in an orderly way.
  • Religion tells about right and wrong and reward and punishment; psychology creates in a person the awareness of the difference between right and wrong.

mcqs.q: What is religion, according to the lesson?
options: A science that studies society and its customs only
An organized system of beliefs and worship whose foundation is the divine message
A collection of stories told by elders
A set of rules made by kings for their people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: an organized system of beliefs and worship founded on the divine message. Religion is not merely customs or stories; its basis is the message sent by the True Owner, and on that basis it organizes man's beliefs and worship.

mcqs.q: On what is the foundation of religion laid?
options: On the wealth of a nation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the divine message. The lesson states clearly that religion is founded on the divine message, and from that foundation it teaches man the principles of living and the difference between right and wrong.

mcqs.q: Psychology is the science of what?
options: The human body and its diseases
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the human mind and behaviour. Psychology studies how a person thinks and behaves, whereas the body, the stars and past events belong to other sciences and are not its subject.

mcqs.q: Psychology helps a person to understand which of the following?
options: The prices of goods in the market
The rules of grammar and spelling
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: thoughts, feelings, emotions and reactions. Psychology deals with the inner working of the mind, so it helps us understand what a person thinks, feels and how he reacts to things around him.

mcqs.q: Which blessing has been given to man, according to the lesson?
options: Great physical strength above all creatures
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: intellect, understanding and perception. The lesson counts this as a special blessing of man, because through it he can think, understand things deeply and judge his surroundings correctly.

mcqs.q: How is religious upbringing different from ordinary upbringing?
options: It is based on principles and teaches a person to understand the beliefs of others correctly, while ordinary upbringing lacks this religious guidance
It only teaches a person to earn more money
It has no rules or principles at all
It teaches a person to avoid meeting other people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: religious upbringing is based on principles and teaches correct understanding of others' beliefs. Ordinary upbringing does not have this religious guidance, so this principled training is what makes religious upbringing distinct.

mcqs.q: What effect does religious upbringing have on a person's thinking?
options: It narrows his thinking to his own group only
It makes him fearful of everyone
It stops him from thinking about others
It broadens his thinking and makes him a friend to every human being
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it broadens his thinking and makes him a friend to every human being. Because religious upbringing rests on principles, it widens a person's outlook instead of narrowing it, and he begins to treat every human kindly.

mcqs.q: What do religion and psychology both basically affect in a person?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his thinking and behaviour. The lesson concludes that religion and psychology basically influence how a person thinks and how he behaves, even though their methods of influence are different.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, what does religion give to a person?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: spiritual peace. Religion gives a person peace of the soul, while understanding the problems of life in an orderly way is the help that psychology provides, so the two should not be confused.

mcqs.q: What does religion tell a person about, according to the lesson?
options: The hidden treasures of the earth
Right and wrong, and reward and punishment
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: right and wrong, and reward and punishment. Religion informs man which deeds are right and which are wrong, and it also tells him that deeds carry reward or punishment, which guides his conduct.

lessons.title: Social and Moral Importance of Religion
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Ethics is the science that tells what is right and what is wrong for an individual or a society. The word "Ethics" comes from the Greek word "Ethos", meaning custom, habit and character. This lesson describes the five types of ethics, the difference between religious and secular ethics, and the great importance of religion in forming the morals of society: religion reduces social evils and teaches love, brotherhood and respect, so religion is not a problem but the solution to problems.

Important Points

  • Religion has an important role in the formation of morals in society.
  • The theory of deontological ethics was presented by the German philosopher Immanuel Kant.
  • The word "secular" was first written by George Jacob Holyoake, the English thinker of secular ethics.
  • Two famous books on secular ethics are Kant's "Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals" and Friedrich Nietzsche's "On the Genealogy of Morals".
  • Religion gives social training, reduces evils like theft, robbery and intoxication, and teaches protection of life, property and honour.
  • Religion teaches charity and forbids hoarding and unlawful profit.

The Five Types of Ethics

TypeMeaning
Virtue EthicsHigh character and honest thinking are necessary for every act.
Consequentialist EthicsThe good or bad result of an act is looked at.
Deontological EthicsEvery act is done under duty and consciousness, and doing justice is necessary.
Religious EthicsHuman action is viewed from the religious point of view and compared with religious teachings and customs.
Secular EthicsActions are judged by human perception, moral conscience, mental ability and reason; connection with a religion is not necessary.

mcqs.q: What is ethics?
options: The science of counting money and goods
The science of the human body
The science that tells what is right and what is wrong for an individual or a society
The science of stars and planets
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the science that tells what is right and what is wrong for an individual or a society. Ethics judges human conduct, so its subject is right and wrong in the life of a person and of the whole society.

mcqs.q: The word “Ethics” comes from the Greek word “Ethos”, which means:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: custom, habit and character. The lesson gives the Greek origin of the word, and these three meanings show that ethics is connected with a person's habits and character, not with wealth or war.

mcqs.q: Who presented the theory of deontological ethics?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Immanuel Kant. The German philosopher Kant presented the deontological theory, in which every act is done under duty and consciousness and doing justice is necessary.

mcqs.q: Who first wrote the word “secular”?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: George Jacob Holyoake. The lesson names this English thinker of secular ethics as the first person who wrote the word 'secular', so the credit for the term belongs to him.

mcqs.q: Which of the following books was written by Friedrich Nietzsche?
options: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: On the Genealogy of Morals. The lesson lists it as one of the two famous books on secular ethics; the 'Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals' belongs to Kant, not to Nietzsche.

mcqs.q: In virtue ethics, what is necessary for every act?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: high character and honest thinking. Virtue ethics judges an act by the character behind it, so a person of high character and honest thinking is required for every act to be morally good.

mcqs.q: In consequentialist ethics, what is looked at?
options: The good or bad result of an act
The age of the person doing the act
The religion of the person's family
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the good or bad result of an act. Consequentialist ethics weighs an action by its outcome, so an act is judged good or bad according to the result it produces.

mcqs.q: In secular ethics, actions are judged by:
options: Human perception, moral conscience, mental ability and reason
The orders of the government only
The wealth and rank of a person
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: human perception, moral conscience, mental ability and reason. In secular ethics a connection with a religion is not necessary; actions are measured by man's own conscience, perception and reasoning.

mcqs.q: Which social evils does religion reduce in society?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: theft, robbery and intoxication. Religion gives social training and teaches protection of life, property and honour, and by doing so it reduces such evils in society.

mcqs.q: What does religion teach about wealth and earning?
options: To hoard wealth and earn unlawful profit
To spend all wealth on luxuries
To do charity, and it forbids hoarding and unlawful profit
To avoid earning anything at all
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: religion teaches charity and forbids hoarding and unlawful profit. This teaching keeps wealth moving in society for the help of others instead of being locked away or earned by wrong means.

lessons.title: Role of Religion in Solving Crises
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

A crisis is a difficult situation that arises in a country or society, such as shortage of things, rising prices or the spread of an epidemic. A national crisis is limited to one country, while a global crisis, like the coronavirus epidemic, affects the whole world. One major cause of crisis is hoarding — collecting and storing things so that an artificial shortage is created and prices rise. Religion gives guidance for solving crises: patience, tolerance, self-reliance, unity, and stopping evils like hoarding.

Important Points

  • Hoarding means storing things to create an artificial shortage in the market so that prices rise.
  • The teacher explained the meaning of crisis with the example of wheat hoarded by landlords.
  • Causes of crises include natural calamities, artificial shortage, hoarding, inflation, epidemics and unlawful activities.
  • Modern-age crises include the coronavirus epidemic, the inflation crisis and the economic crisis.
  • When demand increases compared to supply, the prices of things in the market rise.
  • In the story in the lesson, Sain Dhani's wife sent him to buy flour.
  • Religion teaches fear of the True Owner, patriotism, patience, tolerance, self-reliance and unity for solving crises.
  • In religious books, the solution to every crisis and every problem is present, so religious education helps in solving crises.

mcqs.q: What is a crisis?
options: A difficult situation that arises in a country or society
A happy festival of a nation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a difficult situation that arises in a country or society. Examples given in the lesson are shortage of things, rising prices and the spread of an epidemic, all of which make life difficult for people.

mcqs.q: A crisis that is limited to one country is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a national crisis. A crisis confined within one country is national, while a crisis like the coronavirus epidemic, which affects the whole world, is called a global crisis.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of a global crisis?
options: Shortage of water in one village
Closure of one shop in a market
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the coronavirus epidemic. It spread over the whole world and affected every country, which is exactly what makes a crisis global rather than local or personal.

mcqs.q: Hoarding means:
options: Selling things at very low prices
Giving things free to the poor
Storing things to create an artificial shortage in the market so that prices rise
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: storing things to create an artificial shortage so that prices rise. The hoarder hides goods from the market on purpose, and this artificial shortage is a major cause of crisis for ordinary people.

mcqs.q: With which example did the teacher explain the meaning of crisis in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: wheat hoarded by landlords. The teacher used this example to show how hoarding creates an artificial shortage of a basic food item and turns it into a crisis for the people.

mcqs.q: When demand increases compared to supply, what happens in the market?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: prices of things rise. When more people want a thing than the quantity available in the market, its price goes up, and this is one of the ways a crisis of rising prices begins.

mcqs.q: In the story in the lesson, Sain Dhani's wife sent him to buy:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: flour. The story in the lesson begins with Sain Dhani being sent by his wife to buy flour, and through this simple errand the effect of hoarding and rising prices on a common man is shown.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a cause of crises?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: natural calamities. The lesson lists natural calamities along with artificial shortage, hoarding, inflation, epidemics and unlawful activities as causes of crises, while charity and unity are remedies, not causes.

mcqs.q: Which qualities does religion teach for solving crises?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: patience, tolerance, self-reliance and unity. Together with fear of the True Owner and patriotism, these qualities taught by religion help a society face and solve its crises.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, where is the solution to every crisis and every problem present?
options: In the offices of the government
In the markets of big cities
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in religious books. The lesson states that the solution to every crisis and problem is present in religious books, and that is why religious education helps in solving crises.

lessons.title: Concept of Sin and Crime
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Sin is the violation of the commands of the True Owner or of religious rules, while crime is the violation of the current law of the country or state. A major sin is a great sin for which severe punishment is told in religious books, which is repeated again and again and for which no repentance is made. Forgiveness of sin is possible through repentance, but for crime, prescribed punishment and respect of the law are necessary. Man is called the "home of error" because error can occur from every human being.

Important Points

  • Original sin means the disobedience of Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him), who ate the fruit of the forbidden tree and was sent from Paradise to the earth.
  • Not every crime is a sin, but when a crime becomes severe and is repeated again and again, it becomes a sin.
  • If the criminal does not get punishment, respect for law will not remain in society.
  • Corruption or dishonesty is counted in sins, crimes and major sins — all of these.
  • Society can be saved from crimes and sins by following religious education, respecting the law, giving prescribed punishment, repenting from sins and creating awareness.

Sin in Different Religions

  • In Islam, lying, gossiping, greed, lust, backbiting, ingratitude and drinking alcohol are counted as sins.
  • In Christianity, pride, greed, anger, jealousy, laziness and overeating are sins.
  • In Sanatan Dharma, greed, anger, attachment, pride, jealousy, gambling and usurping others' rights are counted as sins.
  • Acts counted as sin in all religions include telling lies, stealing, greed, lust, anger, jealousy, pride, backbiting, ingratitude, drinking alcohol and usurping others' rights.

mcqs.q: What is sin?
options: The violation of the traffic rules of a city
A mistake made in counting money
The violation of the commands of the True Owner or of religious rules
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the violation of the commands of the True Owner or of religious rules. Sin is judged against religion's commands, whereas breaking the law of the state is a different thing, called crime.

mcqs.q: What is crime?
options: The violation of the current law of the country or state
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the violation of the current law of the country or state. Crime is measured by the law in force, and for crime the prescribed punishment and respect of the law are necessary.

mcqs.q: A major sin is a sin which:
options: Is committed only once in life
Is done by mistake without knowing
Has severe punishment told for it in religious books, is repeated again and again, and no repentance is made for it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a great sin with severe punishment told in religious books, repeated again and again without repentance. All three features together — severity, repetition and lack of repentance — make a sin a major sin.

mcqs.q: Forgiveness of sin is possible through:
options: Paying a fine to the state
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: repentance. The lesson teaches that a sinner can be forgiven when he repents, while for a crime the prescribed punishment and respect of the law are necessary; repentance is the door for sin.

mcqs.q: Why is man called the “home of error”?
options: Because man travels from place to place
Because man forgets his home address
Because error can occur from every human being
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because error can occur from every human being. No person is free from the possibility of mistake, and this common human weakness is why man is called the home of error.

mcqs.q: Original sin means:
options: The first crime recorded by a court
The first lie told by a child
The disobedience of Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him), who ate the fruit of the forbidden tree and was sent from Paradise to the earth
The theft committed in old times
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the disobedience of Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him). He ate the fruit of the forbidden tree and was sent from Paradise to the earth, and this first disobedience is what the term original sin refers to.

mcqs.q: When does a crime become a sin?
options: When it is reported in a newspaper
When it becomes severe and is repeated again and again
When it is done in another country
When only one person knows about it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: when it becomes severe and is repeated again and again. The lesson says that not every crime is a sin, but severity and repetition turn a crime into a sin as well.

mcqs.q: Corruption or dishonesty is counted in:
options: Sins, crimes and major sins — all of these
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: sins, crimes and major sins — all of these. Corruption breaks religious commands, breaks the law of the state, and is a grave act, so the lesson places it in all three categories together.

mcqs.q: In Christianity, which of the following are counted as sins?
options: Pride, greed, anger, jealousy, laziness and overeating
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: pride, greed, anger, jealousy, laziness and overeating. The lesson lists these as sins in Christianity, and several of them, such as greed, anger and pride, are sins in other religions too.

mcqs.q: Which of the following acts is counted as a sin in all religions?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: stealing. The lesson's common list of sins in all religions includes lying, stealing, greed, lust, anger, jealousy, pride, backbiting, ingratitude, drinking alcohol and usurping others' rights.

lessons.title: Jainism (Introduction and Development)
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Jainism has existed since eternity and has been revived from time to time. The founder of its present form is the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar, Mahavira, who started preaching this religion in 569 BC. "Jain" means "conqueror" — one who has controlled his own self and worldly desires. A Tirthankar is a great saint who, after much austerity, attains complete consciousness and shows people the path of liberation. The basic principle of Jainism is ahimsa (non-violence).

Important Points

  • There are twenty-four Tirthankaras of Jainism; the first ten include Rishabha Natha, Ajita Natha, Sambhava Natha, Abhinandana Natha and Sumati Natha.
  • In the fourth century BC, Jainism greatly progressed; in the twelfth century AD its followers settled in many regions of India.
  • Nowadays the followers of Jain Dharma preach their religion in India, Europe, Africa and America.
  • In Jainism, hurting or killing every living being is the greatest sin.

The Two Sects of Jainism

  • Digambar: those who live in natural dress, that is, they have no particular arrangement of clothes.
  • Shwetambar: those who wear white clothes.
  • The difference between the two sects is only this: one adopts natural dress and the other wears white clothes.

mcqs.q: Who is the founder of the present form of Jainism?
options: The twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar, Mahavira
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Mahavira, the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar. Jainism has existed since eternity and was revived from time to time, but the founder of its present form is Mahavira.

mcqs.q: In which year did Mahavira start preaching Jainism?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 569 BC. Mahavira was born in 599 BC and attained nirvana in 527 BC, but the lesson states that he started preaching this religion in 569 BC.

mcqs.q: The word “Jain” means:
options: Conqueror — one who has controlled his own self and worldly desires
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: conqueror — one who has controlled his own self and worldly desires. The victory meant here is not over other people but over one's own self and desires.

mcqs.q: A Tirthankar is a great saint who:
options: Rules a large kingdom with justice
After much austerity attains complete consciousness and shows people the path of liberation
Writes books on the history of religions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a saint who, after much austerity, attains complete consciousness and shows people the path of liberation. This is the lesson's definition of a Tirthankar, of whom Jainism has twenty-four.

mcqs.q: What is the basic principle of Jainism?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: ahimsa, that is, non-violence. The whole teaching of Jainism rests on not hurting any living being, and hurting or killing a living being is its greatest sin.

mcqs.q: How many Tirthankaras are there in Jainism?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: twenty-four. The lesson states that there are twenty-four Tirthankaras of Jainism, the last of whom is Mahavira, and the first ten include Rishabha Natha and others.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is named among the first ten Tirthankaras?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Rishabha Natha. The lesson names Rishabha Natha, Ajita Natha, Sambhava Natha, Abhinandana Natha and Sumati Natha among the first ten, while Mahavira is the twenty-fourth and last.

mcqs.q: In Jainism, the greatest sin is:
options: Hurting or killing every living being
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: hurting or killing every living being. Because ahimsa is the basic principle of Jainism, violence against any living creature is counted as its greatest sin.

mcqs.q: The Digambar sect of Jainism consists of those who:
options: Live in natural dress, having no particular arrangement of clothes
Keep their heads covered with turbans
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: those who live in natural dress with no particular arrangement of clothes. This dress practice is the only difference between the Digambar and the Shwetambar sects.

mcqs.q: The Shwetambar sect of Jainism is known for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: wearing white clothes. The lesson explains that the difference between the two sects of Jainism is only this — one adopts natural dress and the other wears white clothes.

lessons.title: Mahavir
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Mahavira, the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar of Jainism, was born in 599 BC in the village of Kundagrama in Vaishali district of Bihar, in a royal family. His real name was Vardhamana; his father was Siddhartha and his mother Trishala. He did severe austerities in the jungle for twelve years and gained control over his body and soul. His greatest teaching is ahimsa — not hurting any living being. He attained nirvana in 527 BC at Pawapuri, at the age of 72 years.

Important Points

  • According to Mahavira, a person gets sorrows and sufferings because of his karma.
  • Keeping chastity and controlling worldly desires is called Brahmacharya.
  • According to the principle of aparigraha, property beyond need should not be kept; excess earned wealth should be given away in charity.
  • Mahavira's teachings greatly affected the common life of Jains: they practise ahimsa in every act, speak the truth, do not steal, live a life of chastity and give away wealth beyond need in charity.
  • Among Jains, the practice of keeping fasts is very common.

mcqs.q: In which year was Mahavira born?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 599 BC. Mahavira, whose real name was Vardhamana, was born in 599 BC in a royal family, started preaching in 569 BC and attained nirvana in 527 BC.

mcqs.q: Mahavira was born in the village of:
options: Kundagrama in Vaishali district of Bihar
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Kundagrama in Vaishali district of Bihar. He was born there in a royal family; Pawapuri is instead the place where he later attained nirvana.

mcqs.q: What was the real name of Mahavira?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Vardhamana. Siddhartha was his father's name and Trishala his mother's, while Vardhamana was the real name of Mahavira himself, the last Tirthankar of Jainism.

mcqs.q: Who was the father of Mahavira?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Siddhartha. The lesson tells that Mahavira's father was Siddhartha and his mother was Trishala, and he was born in their royal family at Kundagrama.

mcqs.q: For how many years did Mahavira perform severe austerities in the jungle?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: twelve years. Through these long austerities in the jungle Mahavira gained control over his body and soul, after which his teachings, above all ahimsa, spread among the people.

mcqs.q: Mahavira attained nirvana:
options: In 527 BC at Pawapuri, at the age of 72 years
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in 527 BC at Pawapuri at the age of 72 years. The lesson joins these three details together — the year, the place and his age — for the nirvana of Mahavira.

mcqs.q: According to Mahavira, a person gets sorrows and sufferings because of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his karma. Mahavira taught that man's sorrows and sufferings are the result of his own deeds, which is why control over one's actions and desires is so important in his teaching.

mcqs.q: Brahmacharya means:
options: Giving all wealth away at once
Keeping chastity and controlling worldly desires
Keeping fasts for a whole month
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: keeping chastity and controlling worldly desires. Brahmacharya was one of the practices of Mahavira's teaching that Jains follow in their common life.

mcqs.q: According to the principle of aparigraha:
options: A person should collect as much property as possible
Trade should be given up completely
Wealth should be hidden from others
Property beyond need should not be kept, and excess earned wealth should be given away in charity
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: property beyond need should not be kept, and excess wealth should be given in charity. This principle keeps a person free from greed and turns his extra wealth to the help of others.

mcqs.q: Which practice is very common among Jains?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: keeping fasts. The lesson notes that among Jains the practice of keeping fasts is very common, along with ahimsa in every act, truthfulness, not stealing and a life of chastity.

lessons.title: Greatness of the True Owner
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

The True Owner is the Creator and Owner of the whole universe: He is from the beginning and will remain forever, He gives sustenance to every thing according to its need, He is Merciful and Kind, Present and Seeing, One and Only, All-powerful and Wise. Man has been created for the purpose of serving His creation. Every good work should be begun with the name of the True Owner, and thanks for His blessings should be offered by remembering Him, obeying His commands and serving His creation.

Important Points

  • The True Owner nourishes everyone, from the ant to the elephant.
  • In every work begun with the name of the True Owner there is blessing.
  • The benefits of remembering His name are: the heart gets peace, life passes well, a person succeeds in this world and in the hereafter, and the True Owner is pleased.
  • For the True Owner, all human beings are equal; He is Present and Seeing everywhere and is the giver of life to every soul.
  • The surroundings around a person are called the environment.
  • The principles of living, dealing and keeping better relations are called 'values'.
  • The verse 'Awwal Allah Aleem Aala Aalam jo Dhani' is from the poetry of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai.

Serving Creation — The Teaching of Religions

  • According to Islam, the best among people are those who benefit others.
  • According to Christianity, service to humanity is itself service to the True Owner.
  • According to Hindu Dharma, serving others is itself the essence of religion.
  • According to Buddhism, he who lives for others is indeed a human being; Mahatma Gautam Buddha says that he who lives for himself is an animal.

mcqs.q: The True Owner gives sustenance to every thing:
options: Only to those who ask Him daily
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: according to its need. The True Owner is the Creator and Owner of the whole universe, and He nourishes every creature in the measure that it needs.

mcqs.q: For what purpose has man been created, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: for serving His creation. Man's creation is linked with service, and thanks for the True Owner's blessings is offered by remembering Him, obeying His commands and serving His creation.

mcqs.q: The True Owner nourishes everyone, from:
options: The child to the old man
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: from the ant to the elephant. This example shows that no creature is too small or too great for His care; He is the giver of life and sustenance to every soul.

mcqs.q: One of the benefits of remembering the name of the True Owner is:
options: A person becomes famous in the city
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the heart gets peace. The lesson lists the benefits as peace of heart, a life that passes well, success in this world and in the hereafter, and the pleasure of the True Owner.

mcqs.q: The surroundings around a person are called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the environment. The lesson defines the word plainly — everything around a person, his surroundings, is called his environment.

mcqs.q: The principles of living, dealing and keeping better relations are called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: values. Values are the principles by which a person lives, deals with others and keeps better relations, and religions teach these values to their followers.

mcqs.q: The verse ‘Awwal Allah Aleem Aala Aalam jo Dhani’ is from the poetry of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai. The lesson quotes this verse about the True Owner from the poetry of the great Sindhi poet Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai.

mcqs.q: According to Islam, the best among people are those who:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: those who benefit others. Islam's teaching quoted in the lesson measures a person's goodness by the benefit he brings to other people, which is service of creation.

mcqs.q: According to Christianity, service to humanity is itself:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: service to the True Owner. Christianity teaches that serving human beings is not separate from devotion; it is itself counted as service of the True Owner.

mcqs.q: According to Mahatma Gautam Buddha, he who lives only for himself is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: an animal. Buddhism teaches that he who lives for others is indeed a human being, and Buddha said that he who lives only for himself is an animal.

lessons.title: Places of Worship and Methods of Worship of the Main Religions
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

A place of worship is the place where the followers of a religion worship their True Owner. Every religion's place of worship has its own name and structure — mosque, church, temple, pagoda, synagogue and gurdwara — but the purpose of all is to worship the one True Owner. This lesson introduces the places of worship of all the main religions and their methods of worship.

Important Points

  • 'Masjid' means the place of prostration; in a mosque there is a mihrab where the imam stands, and domes and minarets.
  • A church is a rectangular hall with a tall tower or dome, pictures of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) and Hazrat Maryam (peace be upon her), and the sign of the cross on top.
  • A temple is a rectangular hall with one or more rooms where idols are kept; Hindus worship there, and followers of Jainism and Buddhism also worship in temples.
  • In the gurdwara, the Guru Granth Sahib is recited, kirtan is sung, and in the end langar is distributed.

Places and Methods of Worship

ReligionPlace of WorshipMethod of Worship
IslamMosquePrayer five times daily, Friday prayer in congregation, taraweeh and itikaf in Ramadan
ChristianityChurchWorship, reading the holy book and singing holy songs; Sunday is the special day
HinduismTempleWorship morning and evening, reading the shastras and singing aarti
BuddhismPagodaWorship and meditation
JudaismSynagogueWorship three times a day
SikhismGurdwaraRecitation of the Guru Granth Sahib and kirtan

mcqs.q: The word ‘Masjid’ means:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the place of prostration. A mosque is where Muslims prostrate before the True Owner; it has a mihrab where the imam stands, along with domes and minarets.

mcqs.q: In a mosque, the imam stands at the:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the mihrab. The lesson describes the mosque's features — the mihrab is the place where the imam stands to lead the prayer, while domes and minarets are other parts of its structure.

mcqs.q: On top of a church there is the sign of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the cross. A church is a rectangular hall with a tall tower or dome, pictures of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) and Hazrat Maryam (peace be upon her), and the sign of the cross on top.

mcqs.q: Besides Hindus, followers of which religions also worship in temples?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Jainism and Buddhism. A temple is a rectangular hall with rooms where idols are kept; Hindus worship there, and the followers of Jainism and Buddhism also worship in temples.

mcqs.q: In a gurdwara, what is distributed at the end?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: langar. In the gurdwara the Guru Granth Sahib is recited and kirtan is sung, and in the end langar (free food) is distributed among the people present.

mcqs.q: In Islam, prayer is offered in the mosque how many times daily?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: five times. Along with the five daily prayers, the mosque has the Friday prayer in congregation, and taraweeh and itikaf in the month of Ramadan.

mcqs.q: In Christianity, the special day of worship is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Sunday. The lesson's table of worship methods states that Christians worship, read the holy book and sing holy songs in the church, and Sunday is their special day.

mcqs.q: The place of worship of Judaism is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: synagogue. Each religion's place of worship has its own name — mosque, church, temple, pagoda, synagogue and gurdwara — and the synagogue belongs to Judaism.

mcqs.q: In Judaism, worship is performed how many times a day?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: three times a day. The lesson's table states the method of Judaism as worship three times a day in the synagogue, which differs from Islam's five daily prayers.

mcqs.q: In Buddhism, worship and meditation are performed in a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: pagoda. The lesson names the pagoda as the place of worship of Buddhism, where its followers perform worship and meditation.

lessons.title: Concept of Piety, Compassion, Sympathy and Truthfulness in Religions
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Piety means doing good deeds for the True Owner, remaining firm on one's belief in good and bad times, keeping thoughts, actions and behaviour pure, controlling desires and respecting others. Compassion (mercy) is kindness to the poor, orphans, the sick and the needy, while sympathy is feeling others' sorrows as one's own and helping them. Sympathy is the foundation of every religion, but sympathy beyond limits causes harm. A clemency appeal is the request to get a convict's punishment forgiven or reduced.

Important Points

  • In Islam, the measure of a person's superiority is his piety.
  • Alexander the Great willed that after his death his hands be kept outside the shroud, so the world may see that he went from the world empty-handed.
  • The principle is: he who does not show mercy to others will also not be shown mercy.
  • The instruction of sympathy in the holy books is not only with human beings but with all creation — animals, birds and plants too.
  • Benefits of sympathy: love, peace and cooperation increase in society, the needy are helped, and a person progresses morally and spiritually.

Mercy and Sympathy — The Difference

  • Mercy (compassion): kindness to the poor, orphans, the sick and the needy.
  • Sympathy: considering others' sorrow as one's own sorrow and helping them.
  • Sympathy beyond limits causes harm, because the one who receives charity beyond limits becomes habitual of it and goes away from hard work.

mcqs.q: Piety means:
options: Praying loudly so that people can hear
Doing good deeds for the True Owner, remaining firm on belief in good and bad times, and keeping thoughts, actions and behaviour pure
Memorising the names of holy books
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: doing good deeds for the True Owner with firm belief and pure thoughts, actions and behaviour. Piety also includes controlling desires and respecting others, so it covers a person's whole conduct.

mcqs.q: Compassion (mercy) is kindness shown to:
options: Only the rulers of a country
The poor, orphans, the sick and the needy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the poor, orphans, the sick and the needy. The lesson defines mercy or compassion in this way, and separates it from sympathy, which is feeling another's sorrow as one's own.

mcqs.q: Sympathy means:
options: Considering others' sorrow as one's own sorrow and helping them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: considering others' sorrow as one's own and helping them. Sympathy is the foundation of every religion, and its instruction in the holy books extends to all creation, not only human beings.

mcqs.q: A clemency appeal is:
options: An appeal for a new trial in a higher court
A request for employment in a prison
The request to get a convict's punishment forgiven or reduced
An appeal to change a law
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the request to get a convict's punishment forgiven or reduced. It is an act of mercy within the system of justice, asking that punishment be remitted wholly or in part.

mcqs.q: In Islam, the measure of a person's superiority is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his piety. The lesson states that in Islam a person is judged superior not by wealth or lineage but by his piety — his good deeds and purity of conduct.

mcqs.q: Alexander the Great willed that after his death his hands be kept outside the shroud, so that the world may see that:
options: He went from the world empty-handed
He wanted to greet the people
He had hidden treasure in his hands
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he went from the world empty-handed. Even the great conqueror Alexander taught through this will that worldly power and wealth do not go with a person after death.

mcqs.q: The principle taught in the lesson about mercy is: he who does not show mercy to others:
options: Will also not be shown mercy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: will also not be shown mercy. Mercy received depends on mercy given; a person who is hard-hearted towards others cannot expect merciful treatment in return.

mcqs.q: The instruction of sympathy in the holy books is not only with human beings but also with:
options: All creation — animals, birds and plants too
Only with the poor of one's own town
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: all creation — animals, birds and plants too. The lesson widens sympathy beyond mankind to every living thing, which shows how broad the teaching of the holy books is.

mcqs.q: Sympathy beyond limits causes harm because the one who receives charity beyond limits:
options: Becomes habitual of it and goes away from hard work
Saves the money for the future
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he becomes habitual of it and goes away from hard work. That is why the lesson warns that sympathy, though the foundation of every religion, causes harm when it crosses its limits.

mcqs.q: One benefit of sympathy in society is that:
options: Love, peace and cooperation increase in society
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: love, peace and cooperation increase in society. Sympathy also brings help to the needy and makes a person progress morally and spiritually, strengthening the whole society.

lessons.title: Accountability and Its Effect on Human Character
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Accountability means answerability of responsibility: a person accepts responsibility for his actions and gives account of them to the higher authority. Self-accountability is the review a person makes of his own day's deeds before sleeping — the recipe of successful people. Accountability creates the feeling of responsibility, ends corruption and helps institutions achieve their targets. According to all religions, every person will give account of his deeds to the True Owner after death.

Important Points

  • The authority of accountability is with the government, the high authorities, and the supervisors and heads.
  • The head of the household can also do accountability; accountability is necessary at every level — home, office and society.
  • In the hereafter, the True Owner Himself will take accountability from every person for his deeds.

Benefits of Accountability

  • The feeling of responsibility is created in a person.
  • A person performs his duty with heart and soul.
  • Correct decisions are taken according to need.
  • Institutions and employees achieve their prescribed targets.
  • Self-confidence is created and corruption ends.
  • Without accountability, a person would become heedless of his responsibility and corruption would increase in society.

mcqs.q: Accountability means:
options: Counting the money of an institution
Keeping a diary of daily expenses
Answerability of responsibility — a person accepts responsibility for his actions and gives account of them to the higher authority
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: answerability of responsibility before the higher authority. In accountability a person accepts responsibility for his actions and gives an account of them, which keeps his work honest.

mcqs.q: Self-accountability is:
options: The review a person makes of his own day's deeds before sleeping
The audit of a government office
The counting of one's money at night
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the review a person makes of his own day's deeds before sleeping. The lesson calls this nightly review the recipe of successful people, because it corrects a person from within.

mcqs.q: Self-accountability is called the recipe of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: successful people. Reviewing one's own deeds every night before sleeping is presented in the lesson as the practice by which successful people keep improving themselves.

mcqs.q: The authority of accountability is with:
options: The government, the high authorities, and the supervisors and heads
Only the head of the household
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the government, the high authorities, and the supervisors and heads. Accountability works at every level — the head of the household can also do it — so it is not confined to courts or police alone.

mcqs.q: Accountability is necessary at every level, namely:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: home, office and society. The lesson stresses that accountability is necessary at every level of life, and in the hereafter the True Owner Himself will take account from every person.

mcqs.q: In the hereafter, accountability from every person for his deeds will be taken by:
options: The angels in charge of graves only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the True Owner Himself. According to all religions, every person will give account of his deeds to the True Owner after death, which makes accountability a religious duty as well.

mcqs.q: One of the benefits of accountability is that:
options: Work is finished in half the time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: corruption ends. With accountability, the feeling of responsibility is created, duties are done with heart and soul, targets are achieved and corruption is finished.

mcqs.q: Accountability helps institutions and employees to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: achieve their prescribed targets. Because everyone must answer for his work, correct decisions are taken according to need and institutions reach the goals fixed for them.

mcqs.q: Without accountability, a person would become:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: heedless of his responsibility. The lesson warns that without accountability a person stops caring about his duty and corruption increases in society.

mcqs.q: Accountability creates in a person:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the feeling of responsibility. This feeling is listed first among the benefits of accountability, because a responsible person performs his duty with heart and soul.

lessons.title: Importance of Time and Its Observance from the Religious Point of View
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Astronomy is the science of stars and planets, by which the times of worship, festivals and fasts of every religion are prescribed. The natural ways of knowing time are the rising and setting of the sun, the movement of the moon and the earth's revolution around the sun. In Islam, prayer, fasting and Eid rely on the moon (the Hijri lunar calendar); Christianity uses the Christian calendar and Hinduism the Hindu calendar. Observing punctuality — doing every work at its prescribed time — makes a person successful.

Important Points

  • The earth completes one rotation on its axis in 24 hours, by which day and night occur.
  • The earth completes one revolution around the sun in 365 days, by which the year is completed and seasons change.
  • By the movement of the moon, the month is known.
  • Advance news of weather, lunar eclipse and solar eclipse is known through the study of the movement of stars and planets by the experts of astronomy.
  • In Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism also, the times of worship, fasts and festivals are prescribed in the light of astronomy.
  • The earth is a planet.

mcqs.q: Astronomy is the science of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: stars and planets. By astronomy the times of worship, festivals and fasts of every religion are prescribed, so this science of the heavens guides religious timekeeping.

mcqs.q: Day and night occur because the earth:
options: Moves closer to the sun daily
Completes one rotation on its axis in 24 hours
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the earth completes one rotation on its axis in 24 hours. This daily rotation is one of the natural ways of knowing time mentioned in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The earth completes one revolution around the sun in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 365 days. By this revolution the year is completed and the seasons change, while the earth's daily rotation of 24 hours makes day and night.

mcqs.q: The month is known by the movement of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the moon. The lesson lists the natural ways of knowing time: the rising and setting of the sun, the movement of the moon for the month, and the earth's revolution for the year.

mcqs.q: In Islam, prayer, fasting and Eid rely on:
options: The moon — the Hijri lunar calendar
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the moon, that is, the Hijri lunar calendar. Islamic worship, fasting and Eid are fixed by the moon, while Christianity uses the Christian calendar and Hinduism the Hindu calendar.

mcqs.q: Which calendar is used in Christianity?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Christian calendar. The lesson contrasts the calendars of religions: Islam relies on the moon, Christianity uses the Christian calendar and Hinduism the Hindu calendar.

mcqs.q: Advance news of weather, lunar eclipse and solar eclipse is known through:
options: The study of the movement of stars and planets by the experts of astronomy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the study of the movement of stars and planets by astronomy experts. This is one of the practical benefits of astronomy named in the lesson, besides fixing the times of worship and festivals.

mcqs.q: Observing punctuality means:
options: Doing every work quickly, at any time
Doing only one work in a day
Waiting for others to begin first
Doing every work at its prescribed time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: doing every work at its prescribed time. The lesson teaches that observing the times fixed for worship and daily work in the light of religion makes a person successful.

mcqs.q: The earth is a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a planet. The lesson states this simply — the earth is a planet that rotates on its axis in 24 hours and revolves around the sun in 365 days.

mcqs.q: In which religions are the times of worship, fasts and festivals also prescribed in the light of astronomy?
options: In Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism also
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism also. The lesson says that in these religions too, the times of worship, fasts and festivals are fixed by the help of astronomy.

lessons.title: Etiquettes
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Etiquettes are the principles, rules, behaviours and moral ways prescribed for creating better relations in society, practised in daily life during conversation, meeting, gatherings, religious places, business and travel. Acting on etiquettes beautifies a person's personality, increases honour and confidence, and ends hatred and enmity from society. The golden rule of social etiquette is: behave with others in the same way as you want others to behave with you.

Important Points

  • Mobile phone etiquette: in the office, meeting or gathering, keep the phone switched off or on silent; do not keep a loud ringtone; for an urgent call, say sorry and speak in a low voice.
  • On seeing someone in difficulty, help him in every way; help the injured in an accident and help people cross the road.
  • Addressing others: listen attentively and with respect, answer with softness, do not cut in the middle of the talk, control anger, and avoid abusive language and backbiting.
  • Conduct: walk with dignity, stand in a queue and wait for your turn, wear clothes according to the occasion, and offer your seat to the elderly, women and the disabled.
  • Etiquettes everyone should know include saying please and thank you, introducing oneself, shaking hands properly, holding the door open for others, observing punctuality and keeping the environment clean.

Etiquettes of Meeting

  • Introduce yourself: tell your full name and give a brief introduction of yourself.
  • Shake hands warmly and properly — neither press with excessive force nor cause pain.
  • Observe punctuality: reach at the appointed time, do not make anyone wait, and in case of delay, inform by phone.

mcqs.q: The golden rule of social etiquette is:
options: Always speak first in every gathering
Behave with others in the same way as you want others to behave with you
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: behave with others as you want others to behave with you. This single rule sums up social etiquette, because a person who treats others well receives the same treatment in return.

mcqs.q: In an office, meeting or gathering, the mobile phone should be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: switched off or on silent. The lesson's mobile etiquette also says not to keep a loud ringtone, and for an urgent call to say sorry and speak in a low voice.

mcqs.q: If an urgent call must be taken during a gathering, one should:
options: Speak loudly so the call ends quickly
Say sorry and speak in a low voice
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: say sorry and speak in a low voice. This is part of mobile phone etiquette in the lesson, so that the gathering is not disturbed by one's private conversation.

mcqs.q: While another person is speaking, one should:
options: Listen attentively and with respect, and not cut in the middle of the talk
Cut in the middle of the talk
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: listen attentively and with respect without cutting in. The lesson also advises answering with softness, controlling anger, and avoiding abusive language and backbiting.

mcqs.q: To whom should a person offer his seat?
options: To the elderly, women and the disabled
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the elderly, women and the disabled. Offering one's seat to them, walking with dignity and standing in a queue to wait for one's turn are part of good conduct in the lesson.

mcqs.q: When introducing yourself at a meeting, you should:
options: Tell your full name and give a brief introduction of yourself
Read out your whole life history
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: tell your full name and give a brief introduction of yourself. A clear and brief introduction is the first etiquette of meeting given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: A handshake should be:
options: Warm and proper — neither pressed with excessive force nor causing pain
Done with the left hand always
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: warm and proper, without excessive force or pain. The lesson describes the proper handshake as part of the etiquettes of meeting that everyone should know.

mcqs.q: If a person is delayed for an appointed meeting, he should:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: inform by phone. Punctuality means reaching at the appointed time and not making anyone wait, and in case of delay the correct manners are to inform by phone.

mcqs.q: Acting on etiquettes ends which of the following from society?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: hatred and enmity. Etiquettes beautify a person's personality, increase his honour and confidence, and remove hatred and enmity from society.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is among the etiquettes everyone should know?
options: Cutting in the middle of talk
Holding the door open for others
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: holding the door open for others. The lesson's list includes saying please and thank you, introducing oneself, shaking hands properly, observing punctuality and keeping the environment clean.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of Places of Worship
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Religious places are holy places where people go to worship, and they increase peace, brotherhood and respect in society. Every person, majority or minority, has the right to worship according to his belief, and no one should be stopped from coming to a place of worship. Common etiquettes for all places of worship are: switch off the mobile phone, wear appropriate and clean clothes, take off shoes outside, sit silently with manners and respect every religion.

Important Points

  • Mosque: take off shoes, go with ablution, cover the head, do not pass in front of one who is praying and do not dirty the mosque.
  • Temple: take off shoes outside, do not use prasad for personal use, participate in worship silently and do not make noise.
  • Church: remain silent before worship, keep library-like silence, participate in the Sunday 'Holy Communion', give full time to worship and say Amen after prayer.
  • Synagogue: go wearing a kippah (cap), do not eat or drink inside, do not put the holy book on the ground and do not make noise.
  • Buddhist temple: take off shoes, wear appropriate dress, do not touch the idol with feet, bow before the idol and do not make noise.
  • Gurdwara: take off shoes, cover the head with a cloth or turban, remain silent during worship, listen to kirtan with manners and take prasad.
  • For giving something, the right hand should be used.

mcqs.q: A common etiquette for all places of worship is to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: switch off the mobile phone. Other common etiquettes are wearing appropriate and clean clothes, taking off shoes outside, sitting silently with manners and respecting every religion.

mcqs.q: In a mosque, a person should go with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: ablution. The mosque etiquettes in the lesson are to take off shoes, go with ablution, cover the head, not pass in front of one who is praying and not dirty the mosque.

mcqs.q: In a mosque, one should NOT:
options: Pass in front of a person who is praying
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: pass in front of a person who is praying. This disturbs the worshipper, so the lesson lists it among the things to avoid in a mosque.

mcqs.q: In a temple, prasad should not be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: used for personal use. Temple etiquette also includes taking off shoes outside, participating in worship silently and not making noise.

mcqs.q: In a church, after prayer one should say:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Amen. Church etiquette in the lesson includes remaining silent before worship, keeping library-like silence, giving full time to worship and saying Amen after prayer.

mcqs.q: The special Sunday service mentioned for the church is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Holy Communion. The lesson says that in a church one should participate in the Sunday 'Holy Communion'; taraweeh and itikaf belong to the mosque in Ramadan, and kirtan to the gurdwara.

mcqs.q: In a synagogue, one should go wearing a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a kippah, that is, a cap. Synagogue etiquette also includes not eating or drinking inside, not putting the holy book on the ground and not making noise.

mcqs.q: In a synagogue, the holy book should not be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: put on the ground. Keeping the holy book raised and respected is part of synagogue etiquette, along with silence and not eating or drinking inside.

mcqs.q: In a Buddhist temple, one should not touch the idol with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: feet. Buddhist temple etiquette includes taking off shoes, wearing appropriate dress, bowing before the idol, not touching it with the feet and not making noise.

mcqs.q: In a gurdwara, the head should be covered with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a cloth or turban. Gurdwara etiquette is to take off shoes, cover the head, remain silent during worship, listen to kirtan with manners and take prasad.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of Office and Bank
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

An office is the place where government or private work is done, and the work of employees in government institutions is to serve the public. Before going to an office, keep extra photocopies of the required papers and the identity card together and check them before leaving home. A bank deposits bills, provides loans, opens accounts, deposits cheques, deposits and withdraws money, sends money online and runs saving schemes. In a rush, one should wait for one's turn, and on completion of work, say words of thanks.

Important Points

  • Online transfer means sending money from one account to another account through the bank via the internet.
  • A special saving account is opened for students in the bank, which creates the habit of saving in them.
  • Method of paying a bill: fill the challan, go to the relevant counter, stand in the queue and wait for your turn, pay the amount and obtain the receipt.
  • Method of opening an account: meet the bank manager, get full information about the saving schemes, gain satisfaction, get a saving account of your choice opened and act on its instructions.
  • Inside a bank: keep the mobile on silent, do not speak loudly, count the received money standing aside there itself, and approach the cashier if it is less or more.

mcqs.q: The work of employees in government institutions is to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: serve the public. An office is the place where government or private work is done, and government employees are there for the service of the public.

mcqs.q: Before going to an office, one should keep together:
options: Extra photocopies of the required papers and the identity card, checked before leaving home
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: extra photocopies of the required papers and the identity card, checked before leaving home. This preparation saves time and trouble when the office asks for documents.

mcqs.q: Online transfer means:
options: Carrying cash to another city by hand
Exchanging old notes for new ones
Depositing a cheque in any bank
Sending money from one account to another account through the bank via the internet
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: sending money from one account to another through the bank via the internet. It is one of the bank's services listed in the lesson, along with loans, accounts, cheques and saving schemes.

mcqs.q: A special saving account is opened in the bank for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: students. The lesson explains that this special account is opened for students so that the habit of saving is created in them from an early age.

mcqs.q: The special saving account for students creates in them:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the habit of saving. Banks open this account for students precisely so that saving becomes their habit, which helps them in practical life.

mcqs.q: In the method of paying a bill at a bank, the first step is to:
options: Pay the amount at any counter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: fill the challan. After that one goes to the relevant counter, stands in the queue and waits for his turn, pays the amount and obtains the receipt.

mcqs.q: After paying the amount of a bill, one should obtain:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the receipt. Obtaining the receipt is the last step in the method of paying a bill described in the lesson, and it is the proof that the bill has been paid.

mcqs.q: To open a bank account, one should first:
options: Meet the bank manager and get full information about the saving schemes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: meet the bank manager and get full information about the saving schemes. After gaining satisfaction, a person gets a saving account of his choice opened and acts on its instructions.

mcqs.q: Inside a bank, the money received should be:
options: Handed to another customer to count
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: counted standing aside there itself. The lesson also advises keeping the mobile on silent and not speaking loudly inside the bank.

mcqs.q: If the money received at a bank is less or more, one should:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: approach the cashier. Counting the money on the spot and informing the cashier of any difference is part of bank etiquette taught in the lesson.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of Bus Stand, Railway Station and Airport
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

In the old era people travelled on foot or riding animals, but the present era is the era of science and technology, with fast conveyances like buses, trains and aeroplanes. The bus stand serves all people, especially those without their own conveyance; railway travel is the oldest, comfortable means; and air travel is the fastest. Each place has its etiquettes: observe punctuality, stand in a queue, book tickets in advance and take care of fellow passengers.

Important Points

  • Bus stand: reach 5–10 minutes before the bus time, stand in a queue to board, offer your seat to an old or disabled person, book long-journey tickets in advance, and check your luggage before getting down.
  • Railway station: a travel ticket is absolutely essential for entering the station; keep luggage under your own seat or above; do not carry strongly smelling food; take care of the bathroom's cleanliness; do not stare at anyone.
  • Airport: advance booking is necessary; pack luggage completely and get information about the number and weight of bags; reach before the prescribed time, get luggage weighed and checked in, answer the staff politely, follow security instructions, keep the phone switched off and go to the prescribed gate on the boarding announcement.
  • For air travel, a ticket, identity card, passport or other travel documents and complete packing of luggage are necessary.
  • Travel luggage should be necessary and brief.

mcqs.q: In the old era, people travelled:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: on foot or riding animals. The lesson contrasts that slow age with the present era of science and technology, which has fast conveyances like buses, trains and aeroplanes.

mcqs.q: One should reach the bus stand how long before the bus time?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 5–10 minutes before the bus time. Bus stand etiquette also includes standing in a queue to board and offering one's seat to an old or disabled person.

mcqs.q: Before getting down from a bus, one should:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: check one's luggage. The lesson lists this among bus stand etiquettes, along with booking long-journey tickets in advance and caring for fellow passengers.

mcqs.q: For entering a railway station, what is absolutely essential?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a travel ticket. Railway travel is the oldest comfortable means of travel, and the lesson states plainly that a ticket is absolutely essential for entering the station.

mcqs.q: In a train, luggage should be kept:
options: Under one's own seat or above it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: under one's own seat or above it. Railway etiquette also includes not carrying strongly smelling food, caring for the bathroom's cleanliness and not staring at anyone.

mcqs.q: In a train, one should not carry:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: strongly smelling food. Such food troubles fellow passengers, so railway etiquette forbids carrying it during the journey.

mcqs.q: For air travel, what is necessary before the journey?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: advance booking. Air travel is the fastest means of travel, and the lesson makes advance booking necessary, along with complete packing of luggage.

mcqs.q: At the airport, on the boarding announcement one should:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: go to the prescribed gate. Airport etiquette also includes answering the staff politely, following security instructions and keeping the phone switched off.

mcqs.q: Travel luggage should be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: necessary and brief. The lesson advises keeping only needed things in travel luggage, so the journey stays easy for oneself and for fellow passengers.

mcqs.q: Which of the following are necessary for air travel?
options: Ticket, identity card, passport or other travel documents, and complete packing of luggage
A letter from a friend abroad
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: ticket, identity card, passport or other travel documents and completely packed luggage. All of these are named in the lesson as requirements for air travel.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of the Market
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

The basic work of a market is transacting. Demand means the buyers' need for a thing, and supply means the quantity of that thing present in the market; prices are determined by the effect of demand and supply. In the old era, trade was done in markets with paper currency, while the modern market includes buying and selling through computer and smart phone, digital currency, social media and online marketing. Without marketing, business does not succeed, as the examples of Amazon and Daraz show.

Important Points

  • The means of business in the present era are computer and smart phone, digital currency, social media, Google, My Business, Facebook, Market Place and website — a person can buy and sell sitting at home.
  • Through social media, one's thing or service is conveyed to the buyers and business grows; social media is the important source of modern marketing.
  • Through marketing, the real needs of customers are understood and the thing is promoted.
  • Amazon and Daraz began their institutions from a small level and became big through marketing.
  • The province of Sindh is famous in the whole world because of its handicraft.
  • In the coming era, digital currency will take the place of paper currency.
  • Through education and skill, a person can understand the market and achieve success by acting on the principles of marketing.

mcqs.q: The basic work of a market is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: transacting. Buying and selling is the basic work of a market, and its prices are determined by the effect of demand and supply.

mcqs.q: In market terms, demand means:
options: The quantity of a thing present in the market
The buyers' need for a thing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the buyers' need for a thing. Demand is the need of buyers, while supply is the quantity of the thing present in the market; together they determine prices.

mcqs.q: In market terms, supply means:
options: The buyers' need for a thing
The number of shops in a city
The quantity of a thing present in the market
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the quantity of a thing present in the market. Supply and demand together fix prices, as explained at the start of the lesson.

mcqs.q: Prices in the market are determined by:
options: The effect of demand and supply
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the effect of demand and supply. When buyers' need and the quantity available act upon each other, the price of a thing is fixed accordingly.

mcqs.q: In the old era, trade in markets was done with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: paper currency. The modern market, by contrast, includes buying and selling through computer and smart phone, digital currency, social media and online marketing.

mcqs.q: Which institutions began from a small level and became big through marketing?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Amazon and Daraz. The lesson gives them as examples that without marketing business does not succeed; they started small and grew big through marketing.

mcqs.q: Social media is the important source of modern:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: marketing. Through social media a person's thing or service is conveyed to the buyers and business grows, so it is called the important source of modern marketing.

mcqs.q: Through marketing, what is understood?
options: The rules of the market committee
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the real needs of customers. Marketing helps a business understand what customers truly need and then promotes the thing accordingly.

mcqs.q: The province of Sindh is famous in the whole world because of its:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: handicraft. The lesson notes this fame of Sindh while explaining how products reach buyers through the market and marketing.

mcqs.q: In the coming era, what will take the place of paper currency?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: digital currency. The lesson predicts that in the coming era digital currency will replace paper currency, continuing the change from the old market to the modern online market.

lessons.title: Aristotle
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Aristotle, the famous Greek philosopher, was born around 384 BC in Stagira in northern Greece. His father Nicomachus was a royal physician. He entered the school of Plato in Athens, remained associated with teaching, and was the teacher of Alexander the Great. In 335 BC he established his own school in the Lyceum. According to Ptolemy, he has one thousand works, the most important being 'Nicomachean Ethics' in ten parts. He is considered the founder of logic and biology, and his death took place in Chalcis.

Important Points

  • Aristotle worked in logic, physics, meteorology, astronomy, zoology, politics, literature, poetry, aesthetics, ethics and psychology.
  • He acquired his early education from his father; his mother passed away when he was small, and his father died when he was ten years old.
  • At the age of eighteen he went to Athens, which at that time was the centre of knowledge, art and wisdom.
  • He taught Alexander the Great the art of governance and speech, and the lesson that every person is a servant of the True Owner and has the birthright to live a dignified life.
  • Alexander said: 'If Aristotle remains alive, thousands of Alexanders will be prepared, but thousands of Alexanders together cannot prepare one Aristotle.'

Aristotle's Moral Theory

Every person is a seeker of happiness and peace, and real happiness is that which is obtained by doing good deeds. A person's real comfort is not in physical pleasure, but in happiness obtained through rational reasoning; low emotions can be weakened through struggle and rational reasoning.

mcqs.q: Aristotle was born around:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: around 384 BC. Aristotle, the famous Greek philosopher, was born in Stagira in northern Greece, and his father Nicomachus was a royal physician.

mcqs.q: Aristotle was born in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Stagira in northern Greece. He later went to Athens, which at that time was the centre of knowledge, art and wisdom, and entered the school of Plato there.

mcqs.q: Aristotle's father Nicomachus was a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a royal physician. Aristotle acquired his early education from his father; his mother passed away when he was small and his father died when he was ten years old.

mcqs.q: Aristotle entered the school of which philosopher in Athens?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Plato. At the age of eighteen Aristotle went to Athens and entered Plato's school, and he remained associated with teaching there.

mcqs.q: Aristotle was the teacher of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Alexander the Great. Aristotle taught Alexander the art of governance and speech, and the lesson that every person is a servant of the True Owner with the birthright to a dignified life.

mcqs.q: In 335 BC, Aristotle established his own school in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Lyceum. After years of teaching, Aristotle founded his own school there in 335 BC, from where his teaching and writings spread widely.

mcqs.q: Aristotle's most important work, written in ten parts, is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Nicomachean Ethics. According to Ptolemy, Aristotle has one thousand works, and the most important of them is this book on ethics in ten parts.

mcqs.q: Aristotle is considered the founder of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: logic and biology. He worked in many fields — physics, meteorology, astronomy, zoology, politics, literature, poetry, aesthetics, ethics and psychology — but he is counted the founder of logic and biology.

mcqs.q: According to Ptolemy, how many works does Aristotle have?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: one thousand works. The lesson quotes Ptolemy for this number, which shows how vast Aristotle's writing was across many sciences and arts.

mcqs.q: According to Aristotle's moral theory, real happiness is obtained by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: doing good deeds. Aristotle held that every person seeks happiness and peace, but real happiness comes through good deeds and rational reasoning, not through physical pleasure.

lessons.title: German Philosopher Immanuel Kant
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Immanuel Kant, the famous German philosopher, was born around 22 April 1724 AD in Königsberg, Germany, in a poor family whose forefathers had come from Scotland. Of short stature, simple and shy by nature, he met his educational expenses by labour and became a teacher at Königsberg University. After fifteen years of labour he wrote 'Critique of Pure Reason' in 1781 AD, and around 1786 AD 'Critique of Practical Reason'. His famous theory is the deontological moral theory. He died on 12 February 1804 AD in Königsberg, which nowadays is Kaliningrad, a part of Russia.

Important Points

  • Kant worked in philosophy, physics, library, teaching, authorship, mathematics and education.
  • His books include 'Critique of Pure Reason' (1781 AD), 'Critique of Practical Reason' (around 1786 AD) and 'General Natural History and Theory of the Heavens'.
  • He became famous through the epistemological theory of knowledge.
  • In 'Critique of Practical Reason' he stated that the foundation of religion is ethics, and ethics is everlasting, strong and unchangeable.
  • Kant could never marry because of his shy nature and spent his whole life as a bachelor.
  • The deontological moral theory means performing a work that fully meets the moral standard with regular responsibility, keeping one's intention correct without waiting for the result.

mcqs.q: Immanuel Kant was born around:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: around 22 April 1724 AD. Kant was born in Königsberg, Germany, in a poor family; 12 February 1804 is instead the date of his death.

mcqs.q: Kant's forefathers had come to Germany from:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Scotland. The lesson tells that Kant's family was poor and his forefathers had come from Scotland and settled in Königsberg.

mcqs.q: Kant met his educational expenses by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: labour. Kant was of short stature, simple and shy by nature, yet he worked with his own hands to pay for his education and rose to become a teacher.

mcqs.q: Kant became a teacher at:
