mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Königsberg University. The German philosopher taught at the university of his own city, Königsberg, which nowadays is Kaliningrad, a part of Russia.

mcqs.q: ‘Critique of Pure Reason’ was written by Kant in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 1781 AD. Kant wrote it after fifteen years of labour; his 'Critique of Practical Reason' followed around 1786 AD.

mcqs.q: ‘Critique of Practical Reason’ was written around:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: around 1786 AD. In this book Kant stated that the foundation of religion is ethics, and that ethics is everlasting, strong and unchangeable.

mcqs.q: Kant's famous theory is the:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the deontological moral theory. It means performing a work that fully meets the moral standard with regular responsibility, keeping one's intention correct without waiting for the result.

mcqs.q: According to Kant in ‘Critique of Practical Reason’, the foundation of religion is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: ethics. Kant held that ethics is the foundation on which religion rests, and that ethics is everlasting, strong and unchangeable.

mcqs.q: Kant died on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 12 February 1804 AD. He died in Königsberg, the city of his birth and teaching, which is nowadays called Kaliningrad and is a part of Russia.

mcqs.q: Königsberg, the city of Kant, is nowadays called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Kaliningrad, a part of Russia. Kant spent his whole life in Königsberg — born, educated, teaching and dying there — and the city now bears this new name.

lessons.title: Imam Ghazali (Rahmatullah Alaih)
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Imam Ghazali, born in Tabaran in the region of Tus in Iran, belonged to a family whose profession was related to yarn. He studied under Sheikh Ahmad Razkani, then in Jurjan under Imam Abu Nasr Ismaili, and then in Nishapur under Imam-ul-Haramain. Nizam-ul-Mulk appointed him supervisor of Madrasa Nizamia, and in 485 AH the Abbasid Caliph Muqtadi Billah sent him as ambassador to Begum Turkhan Khatun. He used to write sixteen pages daily; his 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' has four volumes, and its abridgement 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' was translated into Sindhi by Mirza Qalich Baig and into English by Claud Field. His final resting place is at Haruniya in Tus.

Important Points

  • During his learning period, thieves stole his luggage with his written copies; the leader of the thieves returned them but taunted him that knowledge locked in books is of no use — after that, Imam Ghazali memorised those lessons.
  • His books include the subjects of philosophy, logic, Kalam and Sufism.
  • 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' describes religious worships, human affairs, habits, the things that destroy a person and the qualities that give salvation.
  • In his last age, he stayed in his ancestral region and remained busy in worship and austerity along with writing and compiling.

Imam Ghazali's Moral Theory

According to Imam Ghazali, ethics or character is the name of a firm and established habit, which can be good character or, because of bad habits, bad character. People whose nature is good can be improved through education and training, but improving people of bad nature is very difficult. He divided people into four kinds with regard to moral character: those with no discernment of right and wrong; those who know evils but do not practise good deeds; those who know evils yet consider them correct and follow them; and those born and raised in a bad environment.

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali was born in:
options: Tabaran in the region of Tus in Iran
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Tabaran in the region of Tus in Iran. His family belonged to that region, and in his last age he returned to his ancestral area and stayed busy in worship and writing.

mcqs.q: The profession of Imam Ghazali's family was related to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: yarn. The lesson tells that Imam Ghazali belonged to a family whose profession was related to yarn, from which his name Ghazali is traditionally linked.

mcqs.q: Nizam-ul-Mulk appointed Imam Ghazali as supervisor of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Madrasa Nizamia. This appointment shows the high rank Imam Ghazali had reached in learning; he had studied under Sheikh Ahmad Razkani, Imam Abu Nasr Ismaili and Imam-ul-Haramain.

mcqs.q: In 485 AH, the Abbasid Caliph Muqtadi Billah sent Imam Ghazali as ambassador to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Begum Turkhan Khatun. Being chosen as the Caliph's ambassador in 485 AH shows the trust and honour Imam Ghazali enjoyed in his time.

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali used to write how many pages daily?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: sixteen pages daily. This steady daily writing produced his many books on philosophy, logic, Kalam and Sufism, including the four-volume 'Ihya Ulum al-Din'.

mcqs.q: ‘Ihya Ulum al-Din’ of Imam Ghazali has:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: four volumes. Its abridgement is 'Kimiya-e-Saadat', which was translated into Sindhi by Mirza Qalich Baig and into English by Claud Field.

mcqs.q: ‘Kimiya-e-Saadat’ is the abridgement of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Ihya Ulum al-Din. 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' describes religious worships, human affairs, habits, the things that destroy a person and the qualities that give salvation.

mcqs.q: Who translated ‘Kimiya-e-Saadat’ into Sindhi?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Mirza Qalich Baig. The English translation of the same book was done by Claud Field, so the two translators should not be confused with each other.

mcqs.q: Who translated ‘Kimiya-e-Saadat’ into English?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Claud Field. The lesson records both translations of Imam Ghazali's abridgement — into Sindhi by Mirza Qalich Baig and into English by Claud Field.

mcqs.q: After the leader of the thieves returned his stolen copies with a taunt, Imam Ghazali:
options: Wrote a complaint to the Caliph
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he memorised those lessons. The thief's taunt — that knowledge locked in books is of no use — taught him to carry his knowledge in his memory rather than only in his luggage.

lessons.title: Florence Nightingale
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Florence Nightingale, the founder of modern nursing, was born on 12 May 1820 AD in the city of Florence in Italy, to William Shore Nightingale and Frances Nightingale. During the Crimean War she went with 38 nurses for the treatment of the war wounded and used to visit their tents at night with a lamp in her hand — that is why she is called the 'Lady with the Lamp'. She began regular nursing education at St. Thomas Nursing School in London, the first secular nursing school of the world, and her book 'Notes on Nursing' was published in 1860 AD. She was awarded the 'Royal Red Cross' in 1883 AD and the 'Order of Merit' in 1907 AD, and passed away on 13 August 1910 AD in Mayfair, London.

Important Points

  • Her parents belonged to a prosperous family and prevented her from adopting nursing because nursing was considered of very low rank in that era.
  • She was educated at home and acquired expertise in German, French and Italian languages as well as arithmetic.
  • Considering marriage proposals an obstacle in her aim, she refused marriage.
  • In 1844 AD she took admission as a nursing student in the Lutheran hospital of Germany; in 1853 AD she was appointed supervisor of the women's hospital on Harley Street, London.

The Environmental Theory

By Florence Nightingale's 'environmental theory' is meant that great importance should be given to a suitable environment during the treatment of the sick: for a patient's recovery, fresh air, clean water, better drainage of water, proper arrangement of the environment, cleanliness of food, and light are essential.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale is known as the founder of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: modern nursing. She raised nursing from a low-ranked occupation to a trained profession, beginning regular nursing education at St. Thomas Nursing School in London.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale was born on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 12 May 1820 AD. She was born in the city of Florence in Italy to William Shore Nightingale and Frances Nightingale; 13 August 1910 is the date of her death.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale was born in the city of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Florence in Italy. Her very name comes from her birth city, though her work and education were later centred in England and Germany.

mcqs.q: During the Crimean War, Florence Nightingale went for the treatment of the war wounded with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 38 nurses. With this team she served the wounded of the Crimean War, and her night rounds among their tents made her famous.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale is called the ‘Lady with the Lamp’ because:
options: She invented a new kind of lamp
She used to visit the tents of the wounded at night with a lamp in her hand
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: she visited the tents of the wounded at night with a lamp in her hand. This nightly service during the Crimean War gave her the famous title 'Lady with the Lamp'.

mcqs.q: Her book ‘Notes on Nursing’ was published in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 1860 AD. In 'Notes on Nursing' she set down her teaching on the care of the sick, the same period in which she began regular nursing education in London.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale began regular nursing education at:
options: St. Thomas Nursing School in London
The women's hospital on Harley Street
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: St. Thomas Nursing School in London. The lesson calls it the first secular nursing school of the world, where she started regular nursing education.

mcqs.q: In 1844 AD, Florence Nightingale took admission as a nursing student in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Lutheran hospital of Germany. She took this step despite her prosperous parents' opposition, because nursing was then considered of very low rank.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale was awarded the ‘Order of Merit’ in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 1907 AD. She had earlier received the 'Royal Red Cross' in 1883 AD, and the 'Order of Merit' followed in 1907, three years before her death in 1910.

mcqs.q: According to Florence Nightingale's environmental theory, which of the following are essential for a patient's recovery?
options: Fresh air, clean water, proper drainage, cleanliness of food and light
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: fresh air, clean water, proper drainage, cleanliness of food and light. Her environmental theory gives great importance to a suitable environment during the treatment of the sick.
